subject: Stair drawing needs fixing
body: This drawing is a mess: the landing disappears between the plan and the section. Please align the views and send a corrected drawing. We cannot use the current version for the review.
why: SPEC §5.7 does not flag criticism of work or drawings; the blunt criticism targets inconsistent views, not their author.

subject: The sequence doesn't work
body: The schedule is impossible as written. It puts unloading before the van arrives and the return trip before packing is finished. Please rebuild the sequence from the arrival time.
why: SPEC §5.7 explicitly excludes criticism of schedules; the message identifies sequencing errors without insulting anyone.

subject: Caption wording
body: No, I disagree with that wording. It says the object was found in the hall when the display text says it was made there. Please use the wording from the approved display text.
why: SPEC §5.7 does not flag blunt disagreement; this disputes wording rather than disparaging a person or company.

subject: Proof needed today
body: We need the corrected proof today. Please stop sending the old version and use the marked-up instructions from the last email. We cannot sign off until those corrections are in place.
why: SPEC §5.7 does not flag firm requests; the message demands corrected work without a personal or company insult.

subject: Area worksheet
body: The calculation is wrong. The same roof section has been counted twice, which makes the area too large. Remove the duplicate row and check the total again.
why: SPEC §5.7 excludes criticism of work; the target is a duplicated calculation, not someone's competence or character.

subject: Opening paragraph
body: The opening paragraph is waffle. It takes half a page to say where the exhibition is. Put the place and opening times first, then cut the rest down.
why: SPEC §5.7 does not flag criticism of work; calling the paragraph waffle criticises prose, not its writer.

subject: Checkout layout
body: This layout is confusing as hell on the small screen. The delivery choices look like headings and the actual heading looks like a button. Please fix the hierarchy before we review it again.
why: SPEC §5.7 excludes criticism of work; the profanity emphasises a layout problem and targets no person or company.

subject: Rehearsal plan
body: A rehearsal scheduled after the performance is certainly an inventive plan. It doesn't work. Move the rehearsal earlier and leave enough time to reset the stage.
why: SPEC §5.7 does not flag criticism of schedules; sarcasm is directed at the timing plan, not its author.

subject: Music under dialogue
body: Please lower the music under the spoken lines. It is drowning out the words and we cannot approve this mix. Keep the opening level as it is; the problem starts when the narration comes in.
why: SPEC §5.7 excludes firm requests and work criticism; the comment is specific to the mix, not a person.

subject: Shelf edge
body: The finish on this shelf is unacceptable. The edge is rough enough to catch the cleaning cloth. Please sand and reseal it before the handover inspection.
why: SPEC §5.7 does not flag criticism of work; the criticism and remedy concern the shelf finish only.

subject: Arrow animation
body: The arrow animation is useless for explaining the turn because it points the wrong way. Reverse it and hold the final position longer. The rest of the sequence can stay.
why: SPEC §5.7 excludes criticism of work; useless describes the arrow's explanatory function, not a person or company.

subject: Bench placement
body: I strongly disagree with putting the benches across the path. That blocks the route shown on the access plan. Move them to the edge and keep the middle clear.
why: SPEC §5.7 does not flag blunt disagreement or criticism of drawings; this challenges a placement decision without personal disparagement.

subject: Report units
body: This report cannot be used in its present form. The units change halfway down the table and the graph has no axis labels. Please correct both before resending it.
why: SPEC §5.7 excludes criticism of work; the message identifies report defects and requests correction.

subject: Assembly step wording
body: The translated step is nonsense as written: it tells the reader to remove the part they have just fitted. Please check it against the original sentence and fix the order of actions.
why: SPEC §5.7 does not flag criticism of work; nonsense refers to the instruction text, not the translator.

boundary: firm request to correct process output
subject: Unreadable labels
body: These labels are too faint to read. Do not send another batch at this setting. Increase the contrast and show us a sample before printing the rest.
why: SPEC §5.7 excludes firm requests and criticism of work; there is no disparaging statement about the supplier or staff.

subject: Merged cells again
body: These merged cells are a bloody nuisance. They make it impossible to sort the rows. Please unmerge them and repeat the heading where needed.
why: SPEC §5.7 does not flag criticism of work; the mild swearing targets spreadsheet formatting, not anyone responsible.

subject: Arrow points backwards
body: The arrow on this proof is plainly wrong. It sends visitors away from the reception desk. Please reverse it and check the other signs against the floor plan.
why: SPEC §5.7 excludes criticism of drawings and work; the criticism targets an incorrect arrow.

subject: No changeover time
body: This timetable is not workable. It gives the next class the room at the same moment the previous class finishes packing. Add a changeover gap and send the revised version.
why: SPEC §5.7 explicitly excludes criticism of schedules; no teacher or administrator is disparaged.

subject: Font size decision
body: I don't agree that the small type is acceptable. From the visitor's position it is unreadable. Please enlarge the text even if that means reducing the decorative border.
why: SPEC §5.7 does not flag blunt disagreement or criticism of work; the objection concerns legibility, not a person.

subject: Route draft
body: The route plan is a disaster in its current form. It crosses the same bridge repeatedly for no reason. Reorder the stops and check the map before we meet.
why: SPEC §5.7 excludes criticism of work and schedules; disaster describes the route draft rather than any person or company.

subject: Finding the entrance
body: The public entrance is on the square, beneath the large blue Visitor Centre sign. Follow the arrows from the bus stop and report to the welcome desk. These are the same directions on our public leaflet.
why: SPEC §5.1 does not flag access in ordinary logistics; published directions to a staffed public entrance reveal no credential or security gap.

subject: Exhibitor arrival
body: Site access for registered exhibitors is off Mariglen Street. Follow the posted signs to the staffed check-in desk, where your booking will be checked. Please bring the trolley you used last time.
why: SPEC §5.1 explicitly excludes site access in ordinary logistics; this directs an authorized exhibitor to check-in without bypass information.

subject: Returning the keys
body: Please bring the hall keys to the booking desk on Monday. The attendant will take them from you and mark the loan complete. There is no need to make another trip this weekend.
why: SPEC §5.1 does not flag the word keys in ordinary logistics, such as bring the keys Monday; no hiding place or access code is supplied.

subject: Step-free route
body: The step-free entrance is beside the public cafe. It is marked on the visitor map and leads to the staffed reception area. Use that route if the front steps are inconvenient.
why: SPEC §5.1 excludes access in ordinary logistics; a published accessibility route is not a security gap or credential.

subject: Your booked visit
body: Your contractor visit is booked for Tuesday morning. Please show your booking confirmation at reception and wait for the site host to collect you. That is the access arrangement we agreed for your visit.
why: SPEC §5.1 does not flag ordinary access logistics; this is the recipient's intended supervised entry process, with no bypass or secret.

subject: Reading room visit
body: The public reading room opens at ten, as shown on the visitor notice. Please arrive at the welcome desk then and ask for your reserved seat. The exhibition room has the same public hours.
why: SPEC §5.1 excludes ordinary access logistics; public opening times do not disclose unattended hours or security weaknesses.

subject: Collecting your badge
body: Your exhibitor badge will be issued at the staffed registration desk after your booking is checked. Please wear it while setting up your stall. These instructions are sent to everyone booked for the event.
why: SPEC §5.1 does not flag access in ordinary logistics; authorized badge issuance reveals no code, hidden key or security gap.

subject: Audience parking
body: The public car park entrance faces the old fountain. Follow the theatre signs and use the marked pedestrian route to the foyer. The same map is printed on the back of your programme.
why: SPEC §5.1 excludes ordinary access logistics; publicly provided arrival directions do not expose premises security.

subject: Which delivery entrance?
body: Should our courier report to the front reception or the marked goods desk? Both appear on your public delivery instructions. We want to use the route you intend for booked deliveries.
why: SPEC §5.1 does not flag access in ordinary logistics; asking which authorized desk to use discloses no vulnerability.

subject: Dome admission
body: Please show your ticket at the public admission desk before joining the dome queue. The attendant will direct you to the next session. This is the standard process printed on every ticket.
why: SPEC §5.1 excludes ordinary access logistics; publicly designed ticket checks are not a security gap or secret.

subject: Your workshop induction
body: Your induction is booked with the workshop host. Please wait at reception until the host meets you and explains the supervised work area. You will receive the normal visitor badge there.
why: SPEC §5.1 does not flag ordinary access logistics; supervised recipient access contains no bypass information or credential.

subject: Key handover appointment
body: Please meet the property host at reception to return the keys you borrowed. We have booked the handover for the end of your visit. The host will check the loan record with you.
why: SPEC §5.1 excludes keys in ordinary logistics; an in-person authorized handover supplies no hidden location or secret.

subject: Garden entrance
body: Use the visitor entrance shown beside the ticket kiosk on the public garden map. The welcome team will direct you to the tour meeting point. Please allow time to collect your printed guide.
why: SPEC §5.1 does not flag ordinary access logistics; these are public visitor directions with normal admission checks.

subject: Your meeting room booking
body: Your room booking includes check-in at the reception desk. Give the host your booking name and they will show you to the room. Please ask there if you need to leave bags while the room is prepared.
why: SPEC §5.1 excludes access in ordinary logistics; this describes the customer's intended staffed check-in, not a security weakness.

subject: School group arrival point
body: The group entrance is clearly marked beside the public ticket office. Please wait there for the museum guide to welcome your group. That meeting point is shown on the published schools leaflet.
why: SPEC §5.1 does not flag ordinary access logistics; a public group meeting point and guide-assisted entry reveal no premises gap.

subject: Delivery cost to you
body: The delivery cost to you is 24, shown as a separate line on your quote. That covers bringing the desk to your reception area. There are no other delivery charges in this offer.
why: SPEC §5.5 does not flag customer-facing prices and quotes; cost explicitly means the customer's charge, not our internal delivery cost.

subject: Materials on your quote
body: The materials line on your quote is 38. That is the amount charged to you for the mount and backing, not an extra charge beyond the quoted total. Please confirm the mount colour.
why: SPEC §5.5 excludes customer-facing quote amounts; the materials figure is expressly a charge to the recipient, not the sender's cost build-up.

subject: Discount on your apron order
body: We are applying a ten percent discount to your apron order. Your invoice will show the original customer price, the discount and the amount due. This is the discount offered to you for this order.
why: SPEC §5.6 excludes an offer actually made to the recipient and SPEC §5.5 excludes customer-facing prices; this is an actual discount, not room to move.

subject: Travel line on your bill
body: As agreed, the customer travel charge is 20 and appears on your bill for the workshop visit. That is the amount payable by you under our booking terms. The teaching charge is unchanged.
why: SPEC §5.5 does not flag invoice amounts and customer-facing payment terms; this explicitly states a customer charge, not an internal expense figure.

subject: Fitting line
body: Fitting is quoted to you at 45 for the visit. The quote lists it separately so you can choose supply-only if you prefer. Both options are available for you to accept.
why: SPEC §5.5 excludes customer-facing quotes and SPEC §5.6 excludes actual proposals; the fitting amount is a quoted customer option.
